server.name: A label for this server in the app. It is not sent in any request.
server.port: The local port the server listens on (127.0.0.1 only). The issuer and endpoint URLs are built from it unless a public URL is set.
server.issuerUrl: The server's base URL: the public URL when one is set, else http://localhost:<port>. Clients use it as the issuer, and its metadata is served at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server.
server.localUrl: Where the server listens on this machine. The public URL forwards here, and it still answers requests sent here directly.
server.authorizationUrl: Where clients send the browser for the authorization code flow (GET /authorize).
server.tokenUrl: Where clients exchange credentials, codes, or refresh tokens for tokens (POST /token).
server.clients: Client ID and secret pairs registered with this server, added here or through dynamic client registration. Import copies one into a new client configuration.
server.clientId: Generated ID a client sends to identify itself to this server.
server.clientSecret: Generated secret a client sends with its client ID to authenticate at the token endpoint.
server.clientName: The client_name the client gave when it registered. It is shown on the consent page.
server.redirectUris: The redirect URIs the client registered. Authorization requests must use one of them exactly.
server.authMethod: How the client authenticates at the token endpoint. none means a public client: it sends only its client ID and must use PKCE.
server.dynamicClient: Registered by the client itself with POST /register (RFC 7591).
server.metadataFetches: Recent fetches of Client ID Metadata Documents, newest first. A client whose client_id is an https URL is identified by the JSON document served at that URL. Documents served from the cache are not listed.
server.users: Accounts that can sign in on the login page when user-based access is on.
server.mcpEndpoint: The MCP endpoint and a command that registers it with Claude Code. Tokens must be issued for the /mcp resource, which MCP clients request automatically.
server.resource: A protected endpoint for testing tokens. Call it with an access token in an Authorization: Bearer header.

serverSettings.publicUrl: For exposing this server through a tunnel or reverse proxy, such as ngrok: the https origin remote clients reach it at. It replaces http://localhost:<port> as the issuer, so the metadata endpoints, protected resource metadata, WWW-Authenticate challenges, token iss, and the audiences the server accepts all use it. Origin only, with no path. The server still listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Changing it changes the issuer, so tokens issued before the change stop validating.
serverSettings.redirectUrlOverride: When set, the server redirects here after authorization instead of to the redirect_uri the client sent. Must be an absolute http(s) URL.
serverSettings.accessTokenExpiry: Lifetime of issued access tokens, in seconds (0 or more). Sets the JWT exp claim and expires_in in the token response.
serverSettings.refreshTokenExpiry: Lifetime of issued refresh tokens, in seconds (0 or more). Refresh tokens are only issued when the scope includes offline_access.
serverSettings.userBased: When on, /authorize shows a login page instead of a consent page, and issued tokens carry the signed-in username.
serverSettings.cimdEnabled: Accept a URL as client_id and fetch the client's metadata document from it (Client ID Metadata Documents). The server's metadata then advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported.
serverSettings.dcrEnabled: Serve POST /register so clients can register themselves (RFC 7591). The server's metadata then advertises a registration_endpoint.
serverSettings.mcpEnabled: Serve a minimal MCP server at /mcp (Streamable HTTP) protected by this server's tokens, so an MCP client can run the whole OAuth flow against it. Its protected resource metadata is served at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp, and the root form then describes /mcp instead of /resource.
serverSettings.cimdAllowHttp: Also accept http:// client ID URLs when the host is localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1], for testing a client on this machine. On by default for new servers, so documents this app serves locally work. The specification requires https.

serverUser.username: The name the user signs in with on the login page. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
serverUser.password: The password the user signs in with. It is stored and shown as plain text, since this is a test tool.
serverUser.userData: Text that GET /resource returns as userData for tokens issued to this user. Leave empty for the default.

clientConfig.name: A label for this configuration in the app. It is not sent in any request.
clientConfig.resourceUrl: A protected resource to test tokens against. Call Resource sends it a GET with the access token. Leave empty for none.
clientConfig.mcpUrl: An MCP endpoint to test tokens against. MCP Probe sends it the MCP requests over POST. Leave empty for none.
clientConfig.tokenForMcp: A token is issued for one audience, so with both URLs set, choose which one is sent as the RFC 8707 resource parameter. A token for one is usually rejected by the other.
clientConfig.discoverFromResource: Finds the authorization server from this URL, so you do not need the issuer. Sends an unauthenticated GET, follows the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728), and fills in the issuer and endpoints.
clientConfig.discoverFromMcp: Finds the authorization server from this URL, so you do not need the issuer. Sends an unauthenticated MCP initialize POST, follows the protected resource metadata (RFC 9728), and fills in the issuer and endpoints.
clientConfig.issuerUrl: Base URL of the authorization server. Metadata is fetched from its RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect well-known URL. When discovery starts from a resource or MCP URL, the issuer is found for you.
clientConfig.useServerMetadata: Fill the issuer, authorization and token URLs from server metadata instead of typing them in. Discovery starts at the URL you ticked, otherwise the resource URL, then the MCP URL, then the issuer.
clientConfig.authorizationUrl: The server's authorization endpoint. The browser is opened here for the authorization code flow.
clientConfig.tokenUrl: The server's token endpoint, where codes, client credentials, and refresh tokens are exchanged for tokens.
clientConfig.clientId: The client ID registered with the authorization server. Sent as client_id.
clientConfig.clientSecret: The client secret registered with the authorization server. Sent as client_secret in the request body. Not used by public clients (Client ID Metadata Document, or Dynamic Client Registration with auth method none).
clientConfig.scopes: Space-separated scopes to request. Include offline_access to get a refresh token from servers that support it.
clientConfig.scopesSupported: Scopes from discovery: the resource's challenge scope, else the resource's scopes_supported, else the server's scopes_supported.
clientConfig.grantType: Authorization Code opens a browser so a user can approve access, then exchanges the code (with PKCE) for tokens. Client Credentials requests a token directly with the client ID and secret, with no user involved.
clientConfig.callbackUrl: The redirect_uri this app listens on for the authorization code. The server must allow it, or redirect here through an override.
clientConfig.extraParams: Extra parameters added to the authorization, token, and client credentials requests, such as audience. A resource entry here replaces the one sent for the resource URL.
clientConfig.metadata: The server's RFC 8414 or OpenID Connect metadata, fetched from the issuer's well-known URL. With a resource or MCP URL, discovery starts there and the trace lists every URL tried.
clientConfig.callResource: Sends a GET to the resource URL with the latest access token as an Authorization: Bearer header and shows the response.
clientConfig.probeMcp: Sends the MCP URL initialize, notifications/initialized and tools/list with the latest access token, showing each step. Stops at the first failure.
clientConfig.probeResult: Each MCP request the probe sent, with the status, the response headers that matter (WWW-Authenticate, Mcp-Session-Id) and the JSON-RPC response. Responses sent as event streams are reduced to the matching message.
clientConfig.resourceResponse: The status, headers, and body the resource returned for the access token.
clientConfig.discoveryTrace: Each URL tried while discovering metadata, with the status it returned and what it meant. A 401 on the resource and 404s on well-known URLs are normal steps.
clientConfig.protectedResourceMetadata: The resource's RFC 9728 metadata, which names the authorization servers that issue tokens for it.
clientConfig.registrationMode: How this client gets its client ID. Pre-registered: you type the ID and secret the server issued. Client ID Metadata Document: the ID is the URL of a JSON document you host, the method the MCP authorization spec recommends. Dynamic Client Registration: this app registers itself at the server's registration endpoint (RFC 7591).
clientConfig.registrationSupport: The registration methods the server advertises in its metadata: client_id_metadata_document_supported and registration_endpoint. A method that is not advertised may still work.
clientConfig.tokenAuthMethod: How the registered client authenticates at the token endpoint. none makes a public client that sends only client_id and relies on PKCE. client_secret_post sends the issued secret in the request body; client_secret_basic sends it in an Authorization: Basic header.
clientConfig.clientIdUrl: The URL of the client metadata document. The server fetches it to learn the client's name and redirect URIs, so the document's client_id must equal this URL. Servers reject URLs with a fragment, credentials, dot segments, or no path.
clientConfig.serveClientMetadata: On by default. The client ID becomes this app's local document URL, http://127.0.0.1:<callback port>/client-metadata/<config id>, filled in when the config is saved. Turn it off to enter the URL of a document you host yourself. While an authorization or token refresh runs, this app serves the generated document at /client-metadata/<config id>, until the token request ends. This only works with authorization servers that can reach 127.0.0.1 and accept http client IDs, such as this app's own server, where Allow http client ID URLs on localhost is on by default for new servers. It never works with remote production servers.
clientConfig.clientMetadataDocument: The document to host at the client ID URL. The redirect URI is this app's callback URL and the client is public (token_endpoint_auth_method none), so authorization uses PKCE and no secret is sent.
clientConfig.verifyDocument: Fetches the client ID URL and applies the rules this app's server uses: no redirects, a size limit, a matching client_id, listed redirect URIs, and no shared secret. It also checks that this app's callback URL is listed. A locally served document is generated instead of fetched.
clientConfig.registerClient: Sends a registration request to the discovered registration endpoint with this configuration's name, this app's callback URL, the authorization code and refresh token grants, the chosen auth method, and the scopes. On success the client ID, and the secret if one was issued, are filled in here; save to keep them. Pull metadata first to discover the endpoint.
clientConfig.registrationResponse: The status, headers, and body the registration endpoint returned. Errors carry an RFC 7591 error code and description.

paramSection.authorize: Parameters sent to the authorization endpoint. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.token: Parameters sent when exchanging the authorization code. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.send: Parameters sent in the client credentials token request. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.
paramSection.refresh: Parameters sent when using the stored refresh token. Uncheck one to leave it out and see how the server reacts.

param.response_type: Always code: asks the server for an authorization code.
param.grant_type: Tells the token endpoint which kind of grant is being exchanged.
param.client_id: Identifies the client to the server.
param.client_secret: Authenticates the client to the server, sent in the request body.
param.redirect_uri: Where the server sends the browser back with the code. The token request must repeat the same value.
param.state: A random value the server echoes back, checked on return to protect against forged callbacks.
param.code_challenge: PKCE: a SHA-256 hash of the code verifier, sent with the authorization request.
param.code_challenge_method: PKCE: how the code challenge was derived. Always S256.
param.code_verifier: PKCE: the secret behind the code challenge, proving the token request comes from the same client.
param.refresh_token: The stored refresh token being exchanged for a new access token.
param.resource: RFC 8707 resource indicator: the resource URL the token is meant for. Servers that bind tokens to a resource may require it or reject it.
